title: Pistachio-crusted salmon
intro: Tender salmon under a crunchy pistachio and lemon zest crust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.

airfryer.t: Preheat the air fryer to 180°C and line the basket with perforated baking paper.

steps.t: Roughly chop the pistachios and mix with the grated lemon zest, parsley, oil, salt and pepper.
Pat the salmon dry, lay it skin side down on the tray and season lightly with salt.
Press the pistachio crust firmly onto the top of the fillets.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily and the crust is golden, 52-55°C in the centre.
steps.label: Oven

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 180°C for 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily.

steps.t: Let it rest, squeeze over the lemon juice and serve.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Chop the pistachios by hand, not in a blender: uneven pieces stay crunchier.
Serve with a fennel and orange salad.

title: Sea bass en papillote
intro: Whole sea bass steamed in its parcel with cherry tomatoes, olives and capers.

ing.n: whole sea bass, gutted, about 400 g each

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C. Rinse the fish and pat dry inside and out.

bbq.t: Set up the barbecue for indirect cooking at about 200°C. Rinse the fish and pat dry.

steps.t: Salt the cavity and fill it with lemon slices, sliced garlic and parsley.
Lay each fish on a large sheet of baking paper and scatter halved tomatoes, olives and capers around it.
Drizzle with oil and wine, then seal the parcels by tightly folding the edges.
Bake until the flesh comes away easily from the backbone.
steps.label: Oven

bbq.t: Use foil instead of paper and cook over indirect heat with the lid closed for 22 minutes.

steps.t: Open the parcels at the table, fillet the fish and serve with its juices.

tips.t: The parcel is ready when it puffs up: open it at the table so the aroma hits everyone.
Serve with boiled potatoes dressed with olive oil and parsley.

title: Mussels marinara
intro: Mussels steamed open over high heat with garlic, wine, cherry tomatoes and parsley.

steps.t: Rinse the mussels in cold water, pull off the beards and scrub the shells; discard open ones that don't close when tapped.
In a wide pot, heat the oil with crushed garlic and the chilli over medium heat until the garlic sizzles.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook until they soften.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Tip in the mussels and wine, cover and cook over high heat, shaking the pot, until they open.
steps.label: Mussels

steps.t: Discard any that stay closed, add parsley and pepper and toss well.
Serve at once in deep bowls with all the juices.

tips.t: Don't add salt: the liquid the mussels release is salty enough.
Shelled, with the strained juices, they dress 320 g spaghetti the same day.
Leave out the tomatoes, just garlic, wine and parsley, for a lighter version.

title: Gambas al ajillo
intro: Prawns sizzling in garlic and chilli olive oil, straight from the tapas bar.

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry with kitchen paper and salt them lightly.
Thinly slice the garlic and crumble the chilli.
In a small clay dish or frying pan, heat the oil with the garlic and chilli over medium-low heat until the garlic is barely golden.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Turn up the heat, add the prawns and cook, stirring, until pink and opaque.
steps.label: Prawns

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add the paprika and parsley and serve right away in the pan, still sizzling.

tips.t: Don't let the garlic brown: once it turns dark, the oil tastes bitter.
Put crusty bread on the table for the oil, and a glass of chilled white wine.

title: Baccalà alla vicentina
intro: Stockfish cooked for hours in milk and olive oil until meltingly soft.

steps.t: Open the stockfish, remove the backbone and pin bones, keep the skin on and cut it into 6-7 cm pieces.
Thinly slice the onions and cook them in 100 ml oil over low heat until soft; add the anchovies and let them melt.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Mix the flour, Parmigiano, parsley, salt and pepper; coat the pieces, fill them with a little onion and close them up.
Arrange the pieces skin side down in a wide pan, side by side, and cover with the rest of the onions.
Pour in the milk and the remaining oil until the fish is covered.
Cook over the lowest heat without stirring: it should barely tremble. Shake the pan now and then.
steps.label: Slow cook

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let it rest: the sauce thickens and the fish absorbs the flavour.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve hot with soft or grilled polenta.

tips.t: Never stir: shake the pan instead, so the pieces stay whole.
Rested overnight in the fridge it's even better: reheat over very low heat.
In Vicenza it's served with white polenta.

title: Teriyaki salmon
intro: Crisp-skinned salmon lacquered in a glossy soy and mirin glaze.

steps.t: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the salmon dry and place it skin side down in a non-stick pan with the oil over medium heat.
Cook until the skin is crisp and the salmon is opaque two thirds of the way up.
steps.label: Skin

steps.t: Turn it over and cook the other side.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Blot off excess fat with kitchen paper, pour in the sauce and simmer, spooning it over the fish, until glossy.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.t: Serve with rice, sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

tips.t: Blot the fat out of the pan before adding the sauce, or the glaze won't cling.
Serve with Japanese rice and blanched spinach dressed with sesame.
With boneless chicken thighs: 6 minutes per side, until 75°C in the centre.

title: Fish moqueca
intro: Brazilian layered fish stew with peppers, tomato and coconut milk.

steps.t: Cut the fish into chunks, season with the lime juice, crushed garlic, salt and pepper and put it in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion, peppers and tomatoes into rings.
In a wide casserole, warm the oil with the paprika and layer in half the vegetables.
Lay the fish and its marinade on top and cover with the rest of the vegetables.
Pour in the coconut milk, cover and cook over medium-low heat until the fish is opaque and flakes.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Uncover, check the salt and cook a little longer to thicken the sauce.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Turn off the heat, scatter with coriander and serve with white rice.

tips.t: Don't stir: just shake the pot so the fish stays in pieces.
Half fish, half peeled prawns: add the prawns for the last 5 minutes.
Serve with white rice and farofa, toasted cassava flour.

title: Sole meunière
intro: Floured, golden sole served with brown butter, lemon and parsley.

ing.n: whole skinned sole, about 300 g each

steps.t: Pat the sole dry, season with salt and pepper, then flour them and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil and 20 g butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Cook the sole dark side down until golden.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Turn carefully and cook the other side until the flesh lifts off the bone.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Move them to warm plates and wipe out the pan with kitchen paper.
Melt the rest of the butter until nutty brown and fragrant, then turn off the heat and add half the lemon's juice and the parsley.
steps.label: Brown butter

steps.t: Spoon the butter over the sole and serve with lemon wedges.

tips.t: Flour at the last moment: if the flour turns damp, the sole won't brown.
Serve with parsley potatoes or buttered spinach.

title: Swordfish alla ghiotta
intro: Swordfish steaks cooked in a Sicilian sauce of olives, capers and raisins.

steps.t: Soak the raisins in warm water, then squeeze them dry.
steps.label: Raisins

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the chopped onion and celery in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Add the halved tomatoes, olives, capers, pine nuts and raisins; salt lightly and cook until the sauce reduces.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the swordfish in the sauce, cover and cook the first side.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Turn the steaks and cook until just opaque in the centre but still moist.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add torn basil and pepper and serve with the sauce.

tips.t: Don't overcook it: take it off as soon as it's opaque in the centre, or swordfish turns dry.
Flake any leftover fish into the sauce and toss it with pasta the next day.

title: Octopus alla luciana
intro: Octopus cooked slowly in its own tomato, olive and caper sauce until tender.

steps.t: In a deep pot, ideally earthenware, heat the oil with crushed garlic and chilli over medium heat.
Add the crushed tomatoes, olives and capers and cook for a few minutes.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the whole octopus in the sauce, cover with a heavy lid and cook over the lowest heat without adding water.
steps.label: Octopus

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: lay the octopus in the sauce, lock the lid and cook 20 minutes at high pressure, then release.

steps.t: Pierce the thickest part with a fork: if it slides in easily it's done, otherwise cook 10 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and let the octopus rest covered in its sauce: it gets even more tender.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Cut the octopus into pieces, return it to the sauce, sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

tips.t: Don't salt: the octopus releases its own salty juices and seasons the sauce.
Serve with slices of toasted country bread (gluten-free if needed).
Leftover sauce makes a great dressing for linguine the next day.
